answers.question: How does the O3 frontend format a date for display according to the user's locale, including showing "Today" for the current day? Point to the documentation and implementation.

paragraphs.text: The O3 frontend formats dates with `formatDate` from `@openmrs/esm-framework`, which uses the browser's `Intl` APIs driven by the currently active i18next locale, and swaps the day number for the localized word "Today" when the date is the current day.

- The recipe `content/en-US/docs/recipes/format-dates.mdx` is the main reference: it documents `formatDate`, `formatPartialDate`, `formatDatetime`, `formatTime`, durations, `isOmrsDateToday`, `parseDate`, `toOmrsIsoString` and locale calendars [1].
- It states the default options are `{ mode: "standard", time: "for today", day: true, month: true, year: true, noToday: false }`, that today renders as `Today` in the locale language, and that `{ time: false }` suppresses the time while `{ noToday: true }` disables the special handling [2].
- Usage examples for `formatDate` / `formatDatetime` and for parsing an OpenMRS date-time string first with `parseDate` are given there [3] and [4].
- The same page documents how locale calendars are registered/overridden with `registerDefaultCalendar`, `getDefaultCalendar` and `convertToLocaleCalendar` [5].
- A French translation of the recipe exists at `content/fr-FR/docs/recipes/format-dates.mdx` [6].
- Auto-generated API docs mirror the same description for `formatDate` [7], listed in the framework API index [8].

- `FormatDateOptions` defines `calendar`, `locale`, `mode` (`standard` / `wide`), `time` (`true | false | 'for today'`), `day`, `month`, `year`, `numberingSystem` and `noToday` [9].
- `defaultOptions` sets `mode: 'standard'`, `time: 'for today'`, `day/month/year: true`, `noToday: false` [10].
- The locale comes from `getLocale()`, which reads `window.i18next.language` and normalizes it to a BCP 47 tag (with an `ht` → `fr-HT` workaround) [11].
- `formatDate` resolves the locale and calendar, then builds an `Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions` with `year: 'numeric'`, `month: 'short'`, `day: '2-digit'` when those parts are enabled [12].
- The "Today" behaviour: `dayjs(date).isToday()` is checked (the `isToday` dayjs plugin is extended at the top of the file packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.ts), and when true and `noToday` is false, `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` with `numeric: 'auto'` formats `0, 'day'`, which yields the localized word for today; the first letter is upper-cased in the locale packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.ts.
- Note the Amharic special case: `noToday` defaults to `true` when the language is `am` packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.ts.
- Otherwise, an `Intl.DateTimeFormat` is used with `formatToParts`; for `en` the locale is switched to `en-GB` so times still show AM/PM packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.ts, English/Amharic standard dates join parts with hyphens `-`, `wide` mode joins with ` — ` packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.ts, and the `era` part is dropped for the Ethiopic calendar packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.ts.
- The time is appended as `", " + formatTime(date)` when `time === true`, or when the date is today and `time === 'for today'` packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.ts. `formatTime` uses `date.toLocaleTimeString` with 2-digit hour/minute, so 12- vs 24-hour follows the locale packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.ts.
- Related helpers: `formatDatetime` delegates to `formatDate` with `time: true` packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.ts; `formatPartialDate` pre-parses year/month-only strings and turns off the missing parts before delegating packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.ts; `isOmrsDateToday` is the public "is it today" check packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.ts; and `getDefaultCalendar` falls back to the calendar the locale resolves to via `Intl.DateTimeFormat(...).resolvedOptions().calendar`, caching it in a registry packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.ts that `registerDefaultCalendar` writes into packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.ts.

The test named "formats 'Today' with respect to the locale" is the ground truth for the Today path: with `en` it expects `Today, 03:22 PM`, and with `sw` / `ru` it expects the localized words (`Leo`, `Сегодня`) packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.test.ts. Locale-specific formatting for non-today dates is covered in the next test (`en` → `09-Dec-2021`, `fr` → `09 déc. 2021`, `sw`, `ru`) packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.test.ts.

Apps import `formatDate` from the framework rather than formatting themselves, e.g. the encounter clinical-view helpers format with `mode: 'wide'` packages/esm-patient-chart-app/src/clinical-views/utils/helpers.ts, the test-results helper forces the time on packages/esm-patient-tests-app/src/test-results/helpers.ts, and print components deliberately pass `noToday: true` so a printed report shows the real date instead of "Today" packages/esm-patient-orders-app/src/print/print.component.tsx.

code: OpenMRS provides several utilities to work with dates. These utilities have been designed with locale sensitivity in mind. Acceptable date formats vary by language and region, and the functions are intended to accommodate that variation.
## Utilities for formatting dates for display
This utility accepts a `Date` object and returns a string. It formats the input date according to the current locale and the given parameters:
The mode parameter can be set to `standard` or `wide`.

For English dates, `standard` mode displays a date such as `16-May-2023`, while `wide` mode displays a date such as `16 — May — 2023`. Other locales may use locale-specific month names, calendars, and punctuation.

By default, `formatDate` uses `{ mode: "standard", time: "for today", day: true, month: true, year: true, noToday: false }`. If the date is today, then `Today` is produced instead of the actual day in the locale language, and the time is appended because the default `time` option is `"for today"`. Pass `{ time: false }` to suppress the time for today's date, or `{ noToday: true }` to format today like any other date.

When the `time` option is set to `true`, the time is appended with a comma and a space, e.g. `16-May-2023, 08:21`. This format agrees with the output of `Date.prototype.toLocaleString` for most locales.

O3 can format dates using locale-specific calendars. The app shell registers implementation-level calendar preferences from the styleguide `preferredCalendar` configuration, and `formatDate` also accepts a `calendar` option for one-off overrides.

Use `registerDefaultCalendar(locale, calendar)` to register a default calendar for a locale, `getDefaultCalendar(locale)` to inspect the resolved calendar, and `convertToLocaleCalendar(date, locale)` when working with `@internationalized/date` calendar values.
